messages:
Maya Chen: Quick sync — I'm pulling together the PRD for next quarter covering API keys, org/project model, RBAC roles, and token scoping. Need alignment on scope, launch criteria, and what gets pushed to later phases. Short list of customer asks: project isolation, scoped keys for third-party integrations, rotation and auditability.

Raj Patel: +1. Strong demand from two customers (FinBank, VideoCorp) for project-level isolation and per-key model restrictions. They also want keys limited by route (embed vs generate) and daily token quotas.

Amanda Li: From a product/acceptance POV, propose:
- Must: create/delete keys via Console + API, list keys with metadata (owner, project, allowed_models, scopes).
- Must: audit log entries for every request with key id, project, route, model.
- Should: rotation endpoint + email/console notif on compromise.

Leo Kim: Runtime note: per-key routing/enforcement will impact caching and batching. Edge case: if we embed per-key restrictions in the runtime, KV-cache hits may drop. MVP option: enforce scopes at the API gateway/proxy layer, emit metrics, then push enforcement into runtime later.

Sarah Nguyen: Rollout idea: hosted API first (beta), then Dedicated customers opt-in, Private (VPC/HSM) later after KMS/HSM integration. Also: for compliance customers, require HSM-wrapped keys by GA.

sec-bot: Security reminder: For private deployments, HSM/KMS integration and key-wrapping are required for FedRAMP/PCI discussions. Also log retention and exportability must be supported.

Raj Patel: Regarding scoped short-lived tokens (delegation flows) — customers ask for token delegation for ephemeral worker services. Acceptance criteria: minted token inherits scopes and TTL, can be revoked independently, and shows parent key in audit trail. Edge cases: chained delegation, token reuse after revoke.

Amanda Li: RBAC acceptance criteria proposal:
- Built-in roles: org_admin, project_admin, developer, auditor.
- Role actions matrix (create key, rotate key, view key, impersonate project) documented.
- Test matrix: negative tests where role lacks permission should return 403 and generate audit event.

Leo Kim: Propagation & invalidation: Hosted: aim for config propagation <5s. Dedicated/on-prem: allow 30–60s due to caching and network partitioning. Document TTL and a force-invalidate API for emergencies.

Sarah Nguyen: QA checklist: rotation flows, revoke and replay attempts, cross-project access tryouts, rate-limit enforcement per-key, telemetry shows per-key token consumption. Include chaos test for delayed propagation.

Maya Chen: Prioritization suggestion (draft):
- M1 (Q3): Key lifecycle + audit + gateway-based scope enforcement + Console UX for keys. Launch criteria: key create/delete, audit logging, basic scope enforcement, 0 CI failures on negative tests.
- M2 (Q4): Org/projects + RBAC + role matrix + policy UI. Launch criteria: role-based access control enforced across Console and API, documented migration steps.
- M3 (Q1 next FY): Short-lived scoped tokens, delegation flows, runtime-enforced model/route restrictions, KMS/HSM GA for private.

Raj Patel: One caveat — eng-runtime has a non-trivial implementation estimate if we require per-key rate limiting and model-level enforcement. We should accept a phased approach: gateway enforcement -> observability -> runtime enforcement.

Amanda Li: Acceptance tests to include in PRD (short list):
- create key -> use key to call generate/embed -> correct allow/deny behavior.
- rotate key -> old key fails after revoke timeframe.
- delegated token -> limited TTL, parent link in logs.
- RBAC negative test matrix.

Leo Kim: I'll draft the propagation/invalidation design doc and include diagrams showing cache tiers and invalidation paths. Will call out perf tradeoffs and a fallback policy.

Maya Chen: Next steps: I'll update PRD draft with these acceptance criteria and the phased roadmap. Action items: @Leo Kim write propagation design (due 1735860000), @Raj Patel estimate runtime work (due 1735870000), @Amanda Li author acceptance test cases (due 1735875000). I'll open the RFC for scope mapping once those are in. Target RFC publish: 1735910000 (one week).

Raj Patel: Sounds good. One more ask: include a migration story for existing API keys (legacy keys with no project) — default to org-level until customer migrates.

Amanda Li: Agreed. Add migration acceptance criteria and a CLI to bulk-assign keys to projects.

Sarah Nguyen: I'll coordinate with customer success to line up early beta users for M1.

Maya Chen: Thanks all — I'll post the updated PRD link here once merged. :thumbsup:
